newsitem.title: UK: European bourses end down on new inflation fears.
newsitem.headline: European bourses end down on new inflation fears.

text.p: European stocks ended the day down on Thursday as an unexpected fall in U.S. unemployment reignited fears of renewed inflationary pressure and higher interest rates.
But the dollar was little changed in late European trading with currency traders preferring to wait for Friday's U.S. retail sales and producer price data for pointers on interest rate prospects.
London and Paris registered losses at the close after the drop in U.S. weekly jobless claims prompted a fall in the bond market and an early sell-off in Wall Street stocks.
London, Europe's biggest bourse, clawed back some of the losses after its initial tumble to end down 0.4 percent, at 3994.7 points on the FTSE index.
"There was a desperate struggle to get back over 4,000 but momentum just faded," one dealer said.

A recent bullish mood in London and other European bourses has been nourished by signs the U.S. economy, after rapid expansion, is slowing to a level where it can sustain inflation-free growth and low interest rates.
Any change in this scenario would be regarded as bad news by markets. Hence investors were worried about the U.S. jobless figures and Friday's American wholesale inflation data for September.

Markets on both sides of the Atlantic were alarmed by the U.S. figures showing the number of Americans signing up for first-time state unemployment benefits fell last week by 22,000. Markets had expected an increase.

The report rekindled jitters about wage-driven inflation, dealt a big blow to the bond market and sent the Dow Jones Industrials down to 5,904.9 points from a close of 5,930.62 before it clawed back some of its losses.
The ripples were felt in Europe. French shares closed sharply lower in line with the poor start in New York and the surprise decline in U.S. unemployment claims, dealers said.
With the blue-chip CAC-40 index down 11.08 points at 2,135.63, investors were now switching their attention to Friday's U.S. data for further clues on interest rate prospects.

Frankfurt floor trade, which closed before the U.S. figures, ended down nearly one percent, depressed by overnight losses on Wall Street and weaker government bonds, which slipped after the Bundesbank left interest rates unchanged.
The 30-share DAX index closed down 22.24 points at 2,680.75, while the IBIS DAX, which records day-long computer dealings, ended down 1.71 points at 2,683.52.
Dealers were divided on the market's next move, but agreed that there was no danger of a major rout. "This is no giant weakness we're seeing here, just some uncertainty," said one Munich dealer.

The dollar edged down against the yen but strengthened slightly against the mark after the Bundesbank, as expected, held interest rates. Some traders saw worries over Yeltsin's health as helping the U.S. currency.

But forex markets were largely hamstrung ahead of the Friday U.S. data release, with dealers eager for clues on whether an interest rate increase could be in the pipeline in the influential American economy.
The U.S. jobless figures confounded expectations of little change from the previous week. "This emphasises the strength of the labour markets in the States," said one analyst.
The dollar jumped briefly in Asia overnight after unfounded rumours of Russian President Boris Yeltsin's death gripped the market.
CURRENCIES at 1600 GMT
The dollar was at 1.5300 marks and 111.26 yen compared with 1.5287 marks and 111.55 yen late in Europe on Wednesday.
STOCK MARKETS CLOSING PRICES
The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares ended 14.6 points lower at 3,994.7.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index finished down 11.08 at 2,135.63.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt closed down 22.24 at 2,680.75.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold closed European trading at $381.95 an ounce, up 50 cents. Silver ended at $5.01, seven cents stronger.
